newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES MIXED IN TIGHT MARKET.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES MIXED IN TIGHT MARKET.

text.p: Short-term trading rates on Zimbabwe's money market were quoted stable to firmer in Tuesday's short market, dealers said.

They added that no maturities were anticipated during the day to lend liquidity to the market and consequently the Reserve Bank had not offered its usual daily treasury bill auction, through which it mops up excess funds.
"But the market is fairly active especially in the 30-day area," one dealer said.

Discount houses were on Tuesday selling treasury bills at a steady 17.55 percent while bankers acceptance bills were indicated firmer at 18.25 percent (buying) from 18.15 percent, but were being sold unchanged at 17.55 percent.

NCDs redeemable after 30, 60 and 90-days were being bought and sold at 19 and 18.25 percent respectively, the same perches they occupied on Monday, but call money edged up to 19 percent from 17.75 percent.
The Reserve Bank said the market closed short of Z$125.9 million on Monday compared to a surplus of Z$137 million on Saturday.
